subject: HIPAA readiness: BAA choices, PHI routing, and next security steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@carepath.health>, security@carepath.health
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: HIPAA readiness: BAA choices, PHI routing, and next security steps

Tom / CarePath team — thanks for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture.

Recap of what we discussed:
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in scope for hosted API controls. We can share the most recent report (redacted) after an NDA.
- BAA: Redwood offers a standard BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. For the hosted endpoint, we require scoped data flows and strong compensating controls; BAAs for hosted customers are evaluated case-by-case.
- PHI boundaries: CarePath indicated ingestion of full PHI for some workflows. Our recommended options:
  * Private (VPC / on-prem) or Dedicated reserved capacity — recommended for workloads where PHI is stored or persisted by the model service.
  * Hosted API — acceptable for PHI if you adopt strict client-side filtering or tokenization and keep model outputs non-persistent; this is subject to legal sign-off and an engineering gating checklist.
- Audit & logs: we support audit logs and KMS integrations on Dedicated/Private; hosted customers get usage logs and anonymized telemetry by default.

Attachments included: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (worksheet we use to collect your security/dataflow answers), redwood_baa_template_v2.pdf (our standard BAA for review), redwood_arch_diagram.png (high-level hosting options).

Proposed next steps (please comment / reprioritize):
1) CarePath to confirm deployment preference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and expected PHI surfaces by EOD 2028-05-12.
2) We initiate the vendor security questionnaire — Priyom will own completion on our side and can help fill in any Redwood-specific answers. (Owner: Priyom)
3) CarePath legal to indicate whether you need a draft BAA; if yes, we’ll send the redwood_baa_template_v2.pdf and propose a 2-week review window. (Owner: CarePath Legal)
4) Mina (engineering) to prepare a short technical note on how PHI would be routed and retained in each deployment mode (Host/Dedicated/Private) and what logging looks like. (Owner: Mina)
5) Exchange SOC 2 report: we can share a redacted copy upon execution of a mutual NDA — let us know who we should send the NDA to.

Open questions we need from you:
- Which concrete PHI fields will be sent to Redwood (examples: patient name, MRN, free-text notes)?
- Does CarePath require data residency (US-only) and do you have a preferred region?
- Are there minimum retention or audit-log retention windows we should account for?

If this looks right I’ll (a) kick off the questionnaire, (b) send the redacted SOC2 once we have an NDA contact, and (c) loop in Legal based on your confirmation about BAA needs.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
D: 415-555-0192 | dylan.brooks@redwood.com

Attachments: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (sheet stub), redwood_baa_template_v2.pdf (pdf stub), redwood_arch_diagram.png (image stub)
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@carepath.health>

Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HIPAA readiness: BAA choices, PHI routing, and next security steps

Dylan — thanks, clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) PHI fields: initial POC will send patient identifiers (name, DOB, MRN), clinical free-text (visit notes), and order codes. We can provide a field-level list by Friday.
2) Residency: yes, US-only required for PHI. Prefer east coast region if possible.
3) BAA: we would like a draft BAA to start redlines; pls send the template.
4) SOC 2: we have an internal requirement to see the latest Type II report. Our security team will execute an NDA if needed.

Action items on our side: we’ll return the field list and confirm whether we can adopt client-side tokenization for the initial POC. For now assume you should treat this as PHI-in-scope and propose Dedicated or Private as the default.

Tom Reynolds
Head of Engineering, CarePath Health
Tom.Reynolds@carepath.health

Talk soon — I’ll mark the task in the deal tracker and schedule a brief follow-up next week to review technical flows.
